brief.objectives: Understand how Gen Z students in Lagos prefer to discover new fashion brands and what emotional triggers influence their purchasing decisions
brief.targetAudience: Students aged 18-24 currently studying at universities in Lagos and Abuja, interested in fashion and lifestyle, active on social media platforms
brief.keyQuestions: How do students currently discover new fashion brands? What are the main pain points? What emotional appeals resonate most? How influential are peer recommendations?

students.name: Chioma Adeyemi
students.bio: Fashion enthusiast, active on TikTok and Instagram. Makes purchasing decisions based on peer recommendations.

students.name: Tunde Okafor
students.bio: Researches consumer behavior, interested in brand strategy. High engagement with emerging brands.

students.name: Blessing Obi
students.bio: Active participant in focus groups, analytical thinker. Strong digital media consumption patterns.

students.name: Kadir Hussein
students.bio: Influencer micro-content creator. Interested in discussing brand evolution and market trends.

students.name: Ada Nwosu
students.bio: Engaged consumer, participates actively in surveys. Thoughtful perspectives on market dynamics.

messages.content: hey! so when last did you buy a new outfit or piece of clothing — like actually pull out your money and pay for something. what was it?
lol okay so like 2 weeks ago I bought a pair of wide leg jeans from a vendor on IG. I'd been eyeing it since December sha
since december? what took you so long to actually buy it
I no guide honestly 😭 but also I kept seeing different styles on my feed and I was like this is pretty dope I need to get this
what changed 2 weeks ago that made you finally go through with it
I saw my coursemate wearing something similar to a hangout and it looked very nice on her, so that pushed me
did you compare it anywhere else before paying this particular vendor, or was it straight to checkout
I checked 2 other pages sha, one was cheaper but the reviews under her post were giving "fabric too thin" I no gree
how much was the price difference between the one you picked and the cheaper option
like 3k difference, 12k vs 9k. I just felt like paying small extra for something that won't disappoint me was worth it
got you. now think of something you almost bought recently but talked yourself out of — what happened there

omo yes, there was this crop top set, really nice, but when I checked the vendor's page well well, all the "customer photos" looked kind of recycled, like reused from a bigger store. that scared me off
interesting — what specifically made you feel the photos were reused
the lighting and background were too consistent across different "customers," like it's the same studio setup. felt fake so I closed the app
thanks so much for your time, really appreciate it, Chioma!
hey Tunde, when last did you buy any clothing item or shoes? walk me through it.
I got a pair of sneakers last month from the thrift market around campus. Just some regular forces.
what made you go to the physical market instead of checking online?
nah, for shoes I have to test the fit. You can't trust these online sizes, plus I need to check the sole to be sure it's durable.
did you end up paying the first price the seller called?
definitely not lol. He called 12k, I priced it down to 8k. It's standard practice, if you don't haggle they'll just cheat you.
was there a point where you almost didn't buy it?
yeah, when he was insisting on 10k, I just walked away. He eventually called me back.
interesting. do you ever buy clothes online then, or is it always physical for you?
I only do online for basic stuff like plain tees from brands I already know. Anything that needs perfect fitting, I'm not risking it.
makes sense. thanks a lot for your time Tunde, really helpful.
hi Amara, tell me about the last piece of clothing or accessory you actually paid for.
I bought a mini bag recently. Saw an influencer carrying it on her page, it had this crazy drip, so I tapped the vendor's tag.
what did you do after getting to the vendor's page? did you buy straight away?
nope, I had to scroll through their older posts first. I was looking for customer tags and checking the comment section.
what exactly were you looking for in the comments?
just checking if anyone was dragging them for late delivery or fake items. You know how IG vendors can be.
and what did you find this time?
mostly positive stuff. A few people complained about the delivery fee, but no one called it a scam, so I felt safe enough to order.
was the price a big factor in your decision?
not really, it was more about credibility. I've fallen for an IG scam before, so I value my peace of mind over saving a few naira.
oh wow, what happened the time you got scammed?
paid 25k for a two-piece set, waited three weeks, and the page literally disappeared. Since then I do proper background checks.
thank you so much Amara, really appreciate you sharing that.

insights.theme: Feed exposure builds desire over time
insights.description: Repeated exposure to a style on social feeds builds desire well before the purchase actually happens.
insights.quote: I kept seeing different styles on my feed and I was like this is pretty dope I need to get this.

insights.theme: Budget delays purchases, not interest
insights.description: Students often want an item for months before buying; the delay is financial, not a lack of desire.
insights.quote: I no guide honestly, that's why it took so long.

insights.theme: Peer styling is the final trigger
insights.description: Seeing someone similar wear an item in person is often the tipping point that turns interest into a purchase.
insights.quote: I saw my coursemate wearing something similar… and it looked very nice on her, so that pushed me.

insights.theme: Quality complaints beat a lower price
insights.description: A cheaper option loses out once reviews mention poor quality; price becomes secondary.
insights.quote: The reviews under her post were giving fabric too thin, I no gree.

insights.theme: Recycled customer photos kill trust
insights.description: Photos that look staged or reused are an instant red flag, even for items the buyer likes.
insights.quote: The lighting and background were too consistent across different customers… felt fake.

insights.theme: Physical inspection is non-negotiable for shoes
insights.description: For footwear, students want to see and touch the item before paying.
insights.quote: For shoes I must see and touch am first… check if the sole is still strong.

insights.theme: In-person bargaining is expected
insights.description: At physical thrift markets, haggling and walking away are normal purchase tactics.
insights.quote: If you no haggle they go just dey smile.

insights.theme: Influencer credibility is vetted in comments
insights.description: Students check prior comments and posts before trusting influencer-promoted items.
insights.quote: I went to check her older posts first, to see if people were complaining.

insights.theme: A past scam permanently increases scrutiny
insights.description: One bad vendor experience changes how students vet every new seller.
insights.quote: Since then I dey very careful.

insights.theme: Family recommendations override reviews
insights.description: A trusted family referral can remove the need for independent verification.
insights.quote: My mother has used her for years, so I trusted her immediately.

insights.theme: Finished work builds trust in new providers
insights.description: For high-risk purchases, seeing a friend's finished item matters more than ratings.
insights.quote: Seeing the actual finished work matters more than anything.

insights.theme: Group buying unlocks higher-priced items
insights.description: Splitting cost with a friend turns an otherwise unaffordable item into a viable purchase.
insights.quote: We split it with my roommate… discount for buying as a pair.

insights.theme: Shared purchases need coordination
insights.description: Group buying adds a coordination cost around timing and preferences.
insights.quote: We discuss well before before we pay.

insights.theme: TikTok trends drive thrift hunting
insights.description: Short-form video is pushing students toward thrift markets for more original pieces.
insights.quote: TikTok honestly, I kept seeing people style thrifted pieces in really creative ways.

insights.theme: Friends act as real-time gatekeepers
insights.description: Friends can veto a purchase in the moment and that veto is usually respected.
insights.quote: Blessing no… I put it back immediately.

insights.theme: Clothing choices signal social status
insights.description: Specific items, especially shoes, signal how seriously someone takes appearance and standing.
insights.quote: People notice shoes especially, I wanted something that put me in a certain category.

insights.theme: Fear of fakes pushes buyers toward originals
insights.description: The risk of being seen in a fake can outweigh the cost savings.
insights.quote: People around here can tell the real from fake almost immediately.

insights.theme: Slow responses are a pre-payment red flag
insights.description: Slow pre-sale replies are treated as a predictor of poor service after payment.
insights.quote: If a vendor is slow to reply before I've even paid them, I already know after payment go worse.

insights.theme: Fast replies and tracking rebuild confidence
insights.description: Quick communication and delivery tracking counteract prior bad experiences.
insights.quote: She replied fast… sends tracking updates once you pay.

insights.theme: Buyers wait for sales to manage budget
insights.description: During tight financial periods, students delay non-urgent purchases for known sale windows.
insights.quote: Anything that's not urgent I just hold… once I see the countdown I know to wait.

insights.theme: Waiting for a sale can mean losing the item
insights.description: Buyers generally accept the trade-off of losing an item when they wait for a better price.
insights.quote: I lost a shirt I liked, but I don't regret waiting.

insights.theme: Unclear returns are a dealbreaker
insights.description: A clear return policy is a first-check requirement after a stressful return experience.
insights.quote: First thing I check is the return policy… if I don't see one clearly stated I just close the page.

insights.theme: Bad sizing drives direct verification
insights.description: After poor fit experiences, students ask vendors for exact measurements.
insights.quote: I now message vendors directly to ask for exact measurements.
